data.title: Cloud Resources Discoverable by Name
data.summary: Cloud storage, function endpoints and container registries were discoverable by guessing names derived from the organisation, exposing which services exist and in some cases their contents.
data.description:
Cloud resources live in global namespaces with predictable patterns: the company name, a product, an environment suffix. Enumerating those combinations is cheap, and third parties publish catalogues of what they find.

Discovery alone is reconnaissance rather than compromise, but it reliably identifies the non-production environments — the ones with weaker credentials, older code and production data copied in for testing.

Where a resource is also readable, discovery and compromise are the same step, and the organisation has no log of the enumeration that preceded it.
data.recommendation:
* Do not treat an unguessable name as a control; apply authentication and network restrictions regardless.
* Include name-based enumeration in your own external assessment, so you find the forgotten resources first.
* Prefer resource names that do not encode the environment where the namespace is public.
* Enable access logging, so attempts against discovered resources are visible.
data.short_recommendation: Do not rely on resource names being unguessable.
